TN-2025-SB2713.aiSummary: The measure changes Sardis town rules, but only if the town government approves it by a two-thirds vote. It updates the town charter by removing old language, letting the board set salaries and meeting dates by ordinance, and changing the mayor and aldermen terms from two years to four years. TN-2025-SB2385.aiSummary: The law changes how Tennessee defines students who are "economically disadvantaged," a term for students from lower-income or certain high-need groups. It also tells the education department to ask the federal government to change the state plan so more students can be counted through direct certification, which means they are found eligible without a household form. Starting with the 2027-2028 school year, school districts that lose funding because fewer students are counted in this group can get extra state money to keep their weighted TISA funding level the same, and that rule ends July 1, 2030.

TN-2025-HB1733.aiSummary: As enacted, the law creates a criminal offense for certain school employees who intentionally bully or cyberbully a student. It also says a teacher or school employee found to have done harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying can be dismissed or suspended. The law applies to acts on or after July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-HB1369.aiSummary: This law requires the health department to make blood lead level testing available for children before they attend public schools and for pregnant women who get WIC food vouchers. If a child or pregnant woman has high lead levels or lead poisoning, the law calls for extra health, school, nutrition, and other support services. It also requires juvenile detention facilities that get federal money to help juveniles in custody who have high lead levels or lead poisoning.
